key_insight: An integer-arithmetic model can certify when moving shared power-of-two scales across an MXFP4 dot-product reduction preserves bitwise binary32 results.
engineering_relevance: Certified scale placement can support correctness-preserving compiler optimizations for low-precision kernels potentially used in FEM surrogates, though no mechanics application is evaluated.
method: Model overflow, NaN, and subnormal rounding with a faithful integer state machine.
Encode rewrite equivalence in QF_LIA and derive a sufficient scale-exponent bound that depends on the reduction tree.
Use certified conditions as static or runtime guards in an MLIR lowering prototype.
evidence_signal: Across tested reduction trees and block lengths up to 64, SMT found counterexamples one exponent step above the bound; on matched queries, cvc5 proved integer encodings in seconds while direct floating-point proofs hit a one-CPU-hour limit even at length 2.
watch_item: Certificates depend on bounded scale codes, supported integer coefficients, and the specified reduction tree; changing these assumptions requires renewed validation.
paper_title: Deciding Scale Placement in MXFP4 Dot Products with Integer Arithmetic
